implementerProof.how: I drove the same surface myself. I built envoy-listener from main c3d09eec and from e55604e4 (git archive, GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/listener), seeded 30,000 records with a seeder I wrote, and measured /proc/<pid>/stat over 60 s. Head idle was 0.0005 cores and base 0.3743, which agrees with the implementer's 0.0003 and 0.44. A signed check_run settled after debounce + one tick, as the implementer saw. I re-ran e2e-local.sh (PASS) and BenchmarkSummary(Idle|Change) -count 3 at base and head; the numbers agree with bench-after/bench-before.

proof.criterion: The summary is recomputed only when an entry changes or falls due (event-driven, due entries in order); no step copies or sorts the whole cache.

observations: A test gap, not a defect: summarizer.pass's handling of a recreated bucket ('if reset' drops the queue and the held set) has no test. A mutant with that branch removed passes GOWORK=off go test ./internal/cistore/ (ok, 15.4 s). On the real binary the mutant's envoy_ci_legacy_records_held goes 2 -> 2 -> 3 across a recreation where head goes 2 -> 0 -> 1. The head's behaviour is correct.
An overrun probe (a throwaway test: the first Publish blocks 20 ticks, tick 50 ms) behaves the same on base and head: one retry at once, then one on each tick, with no burst of catch-up passes.
